text:
lucy: Heads-up: I'm trying to make the ingress lifecycle less leaky. The current 7-phase model is great on paper but terrible in tests and incident triage. Thoughts on collapsing it? :wave:

daniel: Curious what you mean by "collapse". Which phases do you think are noise vs signal?

lucy: The middle-of-the-pipeline transient phases (PREPARE -> QUEUED -> HANDOFF) are usually operational. From a client's POV, they just care if the request is accepted, if streaming has started, or the final outcome.

mina: So ACCEPTED, STREAMING, DONE (with reason) sounds reasonable. But what about reporting backpressure/backoff to clients? We still need that surface.

daniel: Represent backpressure as meta/attributes on ACCEPTED (admission info) and on STREAMING (pressure_hint). Don't make it a state. That keeps the graph tiny and still gives clients hints.

kevin: What about retries? We historically try to resume streams mid-flight which is a major source of dupes. Can we ban mid-stream retries entirely unless the client opted-in?
lucy: Yes. New rule: no automatic mid-stream retries. Retry window is only pre-body (headers) or when a resumable flag is set by client: `x-rw-resumable: 1`. Otherwise post-body failures are terminal.

mina: Pragmatic. Also propose a small trailer contract so consumers have a reliable final signal when streaming: trailer `x-rw-terminal: <OK|UPSTREAM_FAIL|CLIENT_ABORT|TIMEOUT|RATE_LIMIT>` and optional `x-rw-code`. Keep trailer size < 512 bytes.

daniel: Note: some SDKs strip trailers by default (Go http2 client in some versions). We need a compatibility checklist. I can run a quick global check across our SDK matrix.

kevin: Observability: emit one metric per lifecycle transition and attach `terminal_reason` as a label. For traces, set `rw.terminal` tag and a short `rw.checkpoint` integer to correlate streaming progress. Avoid emitting separate metrics for every intermediate admission event to keep cardinality low.

lucy: Agreed. Also add a succinct admission header `x-rw-admit` with values `ok|queued|reject` and optional `x-rw-queue-eta`. This is for clients that want to show "you're in line" UI.

mina: For draining/maintenance: ACCEPTED remains allowed if we can satisfy SLO; otherwise reply 503 with `Retry-After`. Add `x-rw-node-state=draining` for diagnostics.

daniel: Migration: proxies should accept both old and new lifecycle telemetry. Plan: implement edge-side shim that translates old phases into the new three-phase view for 3 months, emit deprecation logs, then flip.

kevin: Security/compat: make sure `x-rw-` headers are only trusted when set by our frontdoor. Downstreams must ignore client-supplied `x-rw-terminal` etc.
lucy: Good call. Also include sample client snippets in RFC for Node and Python showing `x-rw-idempotency` and `x-rw-resumable`. Keep them tiny.

ops-bot: Created ticket INFRA-4021 to track SDK compatibility checks and shim work (https://issues/redwood/INFRA-4021).

mina: Action items: daniel -> SDK trailer compatibility matrix; kevin -> telemetry labels + metric names; lucy -> draft RFC with small state diagram and migration timeline; I'll prototype the admission header in the edge shim.

daniel: I'll also collect a few recent incidents where mid-stream retries caused duplicate side-effects and attach them to the RFC as motivation.
